changed.headline: Because of AI, 52% of students with elevated depressive symptoms who used a generative-AI coaching app for six weeks improved meaningfully, against 32% given care as usual.
Because of AI, primary care teams at Mayo Clinic diagnosed advanced liver disease in about 5 more patients per 1,000 adults who had a routine ECG.
Because of AI, physicians using ambient scribes reported modestly less burnout, exhaustion, and task load in a 238-physician randomized trial.
AI-personalized computer-assisted learning did no better than non-personalized software for 8,647 rural Chinese primary students.
Because of AI, a baby girl was born to a couple who had been told there was no sperm to work with.
Because of AI, 1,660 TB cases were found in Ethiopia between January 2025 and March 2026 in screening programs that had no radiologist to read the X-rays.
Every Cure's AI ranks 75 million drug–disease pairs; its patient wins so far came from clinicians or predate the window.
Because of AI, Northumbrian Water stopped losing about 6.4 million litres of drinking water a day.
Three FireSat satellites launched in July 2026 to spot 5×5 m fires from orbit; no fire-response outcome has been measured yet.
Because of AI, 30 hearing-aid users understood far more words in heavy noise — according to the company that makes the device.
Because of AI, the Hurricane Center called a Category 5 landfall in Jamaica about three days out, while Melissa was still a Category 1.
Because of AI, TB case notifications rose 80% in a tribal district of Chhattisgarh, India, including 20 confirmed cases in people with no symptoms.
A GPT-4o assistant built into the medical record improved Kenyan clinicians' notes and plans but did not reduce treatment failure for 9,691 patients.
A GPT-4o tutor built into a university learning platform was associated with lower grades in a 2,379-student randomized trial.
Because of AI, Swedish mammography screening found 29% more cancers with 44% less radiologist reading time, and 12% fewer cancers surfaced between screens.
Because of AI, about a third of urgent skin-cancer referrals at some NHS hospitals got a same-day all-clear without waiting weeks for a dermatologist.
Because of AI, stroke patients in England were 57% more likely to get a thrombectomy and reached specialist centres 64 minutes faster.
Because of AI, Oman screened 43,000 diabetics for retinopathy, flagged 12,000 for treatment, and cut specialist waiting lists by 87%.
The first generative-AI-discovered drug entered Phase III in September 2026 — no AI-discovered drug has yet been approved anywhere.
An AI stethoscope rolled out to 205 NHS GP practices did not significantly increase heart-failure detection at 12 months.
Because of AI, a man with ALS has spoken with his family and kept working from home for two years through a brain implant, at up to 99% word accuracy.
Because of AI, 284 UCLA clinicians reported modestly lower task load and burnout from a chart summarizer — while saving no time and mostly not recommending it.
Displaying AI deterioration-risk scores on a cardiology ward did not improve patient outcomes across 10,422 admissions.
Because of AI, there were an estimated 841 fewer injury-causing crashes across 270 million driverless miles.

verifications.detail: The sources support operational 24-hour forecasts available in over 150 countries and retrospective forecast evaluation. They do not establish alert-driven actions or measured improvements in human outcomes.

The records support recruiting Phase 3 trials and the stated SOLAIRIA-1 plans, but provide no results, AI provenance, or evidence about approvals of AI-designed antibodies. SOLAIRIA-1 was first posted on 2025-12-11; the entry's published date of 2025-12-03 is its actual study start date.

The preregistered cluster randomized trial supports approximately 26% fewer three-month vascular events and 10 fewer events per 1,000 patients with the AI-containing package. It does not isolate AI's contribution, and the reported benefits predate the current window.

The complete research technical report supports a +0.258 SD mathematics effect for the classroom package, with eight instructional weeks delivered during October–December 2025. It does not establish AI's separate contribution or sustained gains equivalent to actual additional years of schooling.

leads_added: AI-assisted radiographic fracture detection and paediatric ED length of stay, before-after cohort. [Injury](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.injury.2026.113765). Real patients with a named comparison. Missing: full text (the reader returned NOT READ), dates, absolute length-of-stay difference, whether the before-after design is confounded.

AI tool for neurology patient-portal message categorisation and routing, implementation study from January, aimed at response times. [medRxiv](https://www.medrxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.10.19.26365557v2). Real deployment. Missing: full methods (the reader returned the page header and subject list only), end date, comparison period, absolute response-time numbers.

Does AI-powered clinical documentation enhance clinician efficiency? Longitudinal study. [NEJM AI](https://ai.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/AIx2601335?af=R&rss=currentIssue). Compare ambient-scribes-nejm-ai. Missing: full text, dates, comparison, absolute time savings.

AI-enhanced auscultation for left ventricular dysfunction, prospective multicentre validation. [NEJM AI](https://ai.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/AIoa2600258?af=R&rss=currentIssue). Likely diagnostic accuracy only. Missing: any change in care or outcomes.

Flourish, generative-AI mobile mental-health intervention, preregistered RCT, 1,137 unscreened university students, 6 weeks versus care as usual. [PsyArXiv preprint](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/nwz9q_v8/). Read in full and drafted as `flourish-ai-coach-students-rct` (enrolment May–Nov 2025, NCT06668532, meaningful depression improvement 52.3% vs 31.7% among elevated-baseline students). Still missing: peer-reviewed version, the registry record check, an end date for follow-up.

Flourish, generative-AI mobile mental-health intervention, preregistered RCT, 1,137 unscreened university students, 6 weeks versus care as usual. [PsyArXiv preprint](https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/nwz9q_v8/). Randomized with real people; stress, depression and anxiety trajectories favoured Flourish (stress β = −0.03, p = 0.010 per the snippet). Missing: the full text (OSF page is script-rendered; only the abstract was reachable), study dates from methods, absolute symptom-score differences, registration id, peer-reviewed version. Effects look small; may be a candidate once the PDF is read.

Scaling Student Support with Conversational AI, four-year RCT of an AI text-messaging chatbot at a large urban public university. [ERIC ED681875](https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED681875) (EdWorkingPaper 26-1409). Missing: the working paper itself (ERIC fetch failed), outcomes (enrolment or persistence), dates, absolute effects.

Parent-led versus AI-guided dialogic reading in children's e-books, RCT. [BJET](http://dx.doi.org/10.1111/bjet.13615) via ERIC EJ1479944. Missing: full text, dates, effect sizes, setting; likely pre-window.

Teaching Evaluation by AI, randomized field experiment on AI teaching reports for professors, Guangxi University of Foreign Languages. [AEA RCT Registry AEARCTR-0019796](https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/19796). In development, 2026-10-12 to 2027-01-31: a protocol to watch, not a lead for results.

@GoogleDeepMind real capability, outcome not yet measured. once there's a number on the ground (hectares protected, enforcement actions, anything), it earns a row. same bucket as flood hub for now: https://t.co/Swie2LUQlX

@EricTopol @ScienceMagazine @NEJM bench numbers keep improving; we wait for the bedside. closest AI-to-outcome RCTs so far: an AI-ECG screen found advanced liver disease in ~5 more patients per 1,000, and stroke decision support cut repeat strokes/MIs/vascular deaths by 10 per 1,000. https://t.co/ovxmID4zA1

@BoWang87 agreed on urgency, and on 'we still have to prove it'. for the record: no AI-discovered drug has been approved anywhere yet. the first generative-AI-discovered one (rentosertib, IPF) entered phase 3 in september 2026. our running not-yet list: https://t.co/yS15K7A9M4

@CBSMornings @celinegounder different job (5-year risk vs reading today's mammogram), but the biggest measured win in breast screening so far is on the reading side: sweden's MASAI trial found 29% more cancers with 44% less radiologist reading time, 12% fewer interval cancers. https://t.co/nZwykyY1KC

@thesupermannx harvard's study is real but small: 194 students, one course. term-long RCTs are messier: a GPT-4o tutor in a university platform was tied to lower grades (n=2,379); a gemini bundle in sierra leone moved math +0.26 SD in 8 weeks. both signs exist. https://t.co/H31gR6dAEW

@cgnorthcutt two term-scale RCTs, mixed signs: a gemini tutoring bundle in sierra leone moved math +0.26 SD in 8 weeks; a GPT-4o tutor inside a US university platform was tied to lower grades, n=2,379. one-hour and term-long gains may be different animals. https://t.co/H31gR6dAEW

@semafor for scale: over its first 270M driverless miles waymo logged an estimated 841 fewer injury crashes than human drivers would have, about 82% fewer. company-reported data, so we grade the evidence C, but the gap is not subtle. https://t.co/0rIsGnw4Xy

@jillnephew @davegoldblatt @azeem @ExponentialView three for frontier llms, and 14 for narrow AIs. you can filter for it: https://t.co/lwwD3yqvYP. LLMs are all modest (two scribe RCTs on clinician burnout, one bundled Gemini tutoring RCT). Two of the five nulls are LLMs too. The hard-outcome evidence is almost all narrow models
